title: Typische Vertikalklitterung als Darstellung des Dada Baargeld, 1920
lede: Cologne Dadaist Johannes Theodor Baargeld pastes a photograph of his own capped head on a reproduction of the Venus de Milo’s torso, and leaves the cut edges in view.
summary: A cut photograph of a young man’s head on a classical marble torso, alone on yellowed paper. Baargeld, Cologne, 1920.

source.label: Wikimedia Commons: Baargeld, Typische Vertikalklitterung als Darstellung des Dada Baargeld (Kunsthaus Zürich)

creator.name: Johannes Theodor Baargeld (Alfred Emanuel Ferdinand Gruenwald, 1892–1927)

evidence.note: Inspected the Commons image (1438 × 1800 px original, viewed at 1200 px). Commons describes it as the Kunsthaus Zürich, Graphische Sammlung, sheet, cropped, and takes it from a Cologne cemetery-society website, not from the museum. No Kunsthaus inventory number was checked.

styles.note: A Dada photomontage: press and studio photographs cut and joined so that the scale and the cut edges show. Partial fit: it has no type.

context: Commons records the work as *Typical Vertical Mess as Depiction of the Dada Baargeld*, 1920, Kunsthaus Zürich, Graphische Sammlung, with the license PD-Art (PD-old-auto-expired, death year 1927). [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Johannes_Theodor_Baargeld_%E2%80%93_Typische_Vertikalklitterung_als_Darstellung_des_Dada_Baargeld_-_1920.jpg).

An exhibition caption gives the medium as photomontage, 37.1 × 31 cm, Kunsthaus Zürich, Grafische Sammlung. [Art Blart](https://artblart.com/tag/typical-vertical-mess-as-depiction-of-the-dada-baargeld/). MoMA used the work in the audio guide of its Dada exhibition. [MoMA audio](https://www.moma.org/audio/playlist/198/2636).
Baargeld founded Cologne Dada with Max Ernst in 1919–1920. [Wikipedia: Johannes Theodor Baargeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Theodor_Baargeld).
observed: A black-and-white photograph of a young man’s face under a peaked cap is cut along the jaw and neck and laid on a photograph of a classical marble torso with broken arms.
The face is warmer and smoother in tone than the grey, pitted marble, so the join is plain.
The torso stands on a cut photograph of a cloth-draped plinth, whose trapezoid edge is clearly cut.
The montage sits in the middle of a large sheet of yellowed paper with stains and creases. A small signature, “zobaargeld”, is written at lower right.
There is no type and no second color.
interpretation: The work shows the photomontage branch of Dada at its plainest: two photographs, one cut, and a joke about the classical ideal. The empty sheet makes the cut more visible than in the crowded Berlin montages.
borrow: Join two black-and-white photographs at one clean cut, and let the difference in tone show the join.
Place one small montage in a large empty field of warm paper.

images.alt: Photomontage on yellowed paper: the head of a young man in a peaked cap is pasted on the photographed marble torso of the Venus de Milo, which stands on a cut photograph of a draped plinth.
images.caption: Johannes Theodor Baargeld, *Typische Vertikalklitterung als Darstellung des Dada Baargeld*, 1920. Kunsthaus Zürich, Graphische Sammlung. Cropped image via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Johannes_Theodor_Baargeld_%E2%80%93_Typische_Vertikalklitterung_als_Darstellung_des_Dada_Baargeld_-_1920.jpg), PD-Art.

rights.statement: Commons tags the image PD-Art (PD-old-auto-expired). Baargeld, a German author, died in 1927, so the montage is public domain in Germany. It was made in 1920. The photographs in it are a portrait of Baargeld and a reproduction of an ancient statue; their photographers are not named, and any term for a pre-1927 anonymous photograph has expired. In the United States the work is public domain in both cases: if published before 1931 the term has expired, and if unpublished the term of life plus 70 years ended in 1997.
